97	def encode(value: Any) -> Any:
98	    """A contract value as JSON data, the inverse of `decode`."""
99	    if dataclasses.is_dataclass(value) and not isinstance(value, type):
100	        return {f.name: encode(getattr(value, f.name)) for f in dataclasses.fields(value)}
101	    if isinstance(value, Mapping):
102	        return {encode(k): encode(v) for k, v in value.items()}
103	    if isinstance(value, (list, tuple, np.ndarray)):
104	        return [encode(v) for v in value]
105	    if isinstance(value, np.generic):
106	        return value.item()
107	    return _encode_scalar(value)

111	    if isinstance(value, Path):

120	# ------------------------------------------------------------------- JSON Schema (a subset)
121	_JSON_TYPES: dict[str, tuple[type, ...]] = {
122	    "object": (dict,),
123	    "array": (list,),
124	    "string": (str,),
125	    "integer": (int,),
126	    "number": (int, float),
127	    "boolean": (bool,),
128	    "null": (type(None),),
129	}

132	def errors(instance: Any, rules: Mapping[str, Any], where: str = "$") -> list[str]:
133	    """Every way `instance` breaks `rules`: type, enum, const, minimum, maximum, minItems,
134	    maxItems, items, properties, required, additionalProperties, anyOf, and `$ref` to another
135	    folder's schema by name (`"$ref": "core.TeamSpec"`, or one of its properties with
136	    `"$ref": "core.Policy#calls"`)."""
137	    if "$ref" in rules:
138	        folder, _, prop = rules["$ref"].partition("#")
139	        target = schema(folder)
140	        return errors(instance, target["properties"][prop] if prop else target, where)
141	    if "anyOf" in rules:
142	        if all(errors(instance, option, where) for option in rules["anyOf"]):
143	            return [f"{where}: matches no anyOf option"]
144	        return []
145	    if "type" in rules and not _type_ok(instance, rules["type"]):
146	        return [f"{where}: {instance!r} is not {rules['type']}"]
147	    found = _value_errors(instance, rules, where)
148	    if isinstance(instance, list):
149	        found += _array_errors(instance, rules, where)
150	    if isinstance(instance, dict):
151	        found += _object_errors(instance, rules, where)
152	    return found
153	
154	
155	def _type_ok(instance: Any, wanted: str | list[str]) -> bool:
156	    names = [wanted] if isinstance(wanted, str) else wanted
157	    if isinstance(instance, bool):
158	        return "boolean" in names
159	    return any(isinstance(instance, _JSON_TYPES[n]) for n in names)
160

162	def _value_errors(instance: Any, rules: Mapping[str, Any], where: str) -> list[str]:
163	    found = []
164	    if "enum" in rules and instance not in rules["enum"]:
165	        found.append(f"{where}: {instance!r} not in {rules['enum']}")
166	    if "const" in rules and instance != rules["const"]:
167	        found.append(f"{where}: {instance!r} != {rules['const']!r}")
168	    if "minimum" in rules and instance < rules["minimum"]:
169	        found.append(f"{where}: {instance!r} < {rules['minimum']}")
170	    if "maximum" in rules and instance > rules["maximum"]:
171	        found.append(f"{where}: {instance!r} > {rules['maximum']}")
172	    return found
173	
174	
175	def _array_errors(instance: list[Any], rules: Mapping[str, Any], where: str) -> list[str]:
176	    found = []
177	    if len(instance) < rules.get("minItems", 0):
178	        found.append(f"{where}: fewer than {rules['minItems']} items")
179	    if len(instance) > rules.get("maxItems", len(instance)):
180	        found.append(f"{where}: more than {rules['maxItems']} items")
181	    for i, item in enumerate(instance):
182	        found += errors(item, rules.get("items", {}), f"{where}[{i}]")
183	    return found
184	
185	
186	def _object_errors(instance: dict[str, Any], rules: Mapping[str, Any], where: str) -> list[str]:
187	    props = rules.get("properties", {})
188	    found = [f"{where}: missing {k!r}" for k in rules.get("required", []) if k not in instance]
189	    for key, value in instance.items():
190	        if key in props:
191	            found += errors(value, props[key], f"{where}.{key}")
192	        elif rules.get("additionalProperties", True) is False:
193	            found.append(f"{where}: unexpected {key!r}")
194	        elif isinstance(rules.get("additionalProperties"), dict):
195	            found += errors(value, rules["additionalProperties"], f"{where}.{key}")
196	    return found

199	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ decoding to contract types
200	def decode(tp: Any, data: Any) -> Any:
201	    """`data` (parsed JSON) as an instance of the contract type `tp`; TypeError if it isn't one."""
202	    if isinstance(tp, typing.TypeAliasType):
203	        tp = tp.__value__
204	    if tp is Any or tp is object:
205	        return data
206	    decoder = next((d for test, d in _DECODERS if test(tp)), _decode_scalar)
207	    return decoder(tp, data)
208	
209	
210	def _decode_dataclass(tp: type, data: Any) -> Any:
211	    fields = {f.name: f for f in dataclasses.fields(tp)}
212	    required = {
213	        n
214	        for n, f in fields.items()
215	        if f.default is dataclasses.MISSING and f.default_factory is dataclasses.MISSING
216	    }
217	    if not isinstance(data, dict) or not required <= data.keys() <= fields.keys():
218	        raise TypeError(f"{tp.__name__} needs an object of {sorted(fields)}, got {data!r}")
219	    hints = typing.get_type_hints(tp)
220	    return tp(**{k: decode(hints[k], v) for k, v in data.items()})
221	
222	
223	def _decode_union(tp: Any, data: Any) -> Any:
224	    options = typing.get_args(tp)
225	    if data is None and type(None) in options:
226	        return None
227	    problems = []
228	    for option in (o for o in options if o is not type(None)):
229	        try:
230	            return decode(option, data)
231	        except TypeError as exc:
232	            problems.append(str(exc))
233	    raise TypeError(f"{data!r} matches no option: {problems}")
234	
235	
236	def _decode_literal(tp: Any, data: Any) -> Any:
237	    if data not in typing.get_args(tp):
238	        raise TypeError(f"{data!r} is not one of {typing.get_args(tp)}")
239	    return data
240	
241	
242	def _is_array(tp: Any) -> bool:
243	    """`np.ndarray`, `np.ndarray[...]`, or a subscripted alias of it such as `NDArray[...]`."""
244	    origin = typing.get_origin(tp)
245	    if isinstance(origin, typing.TypeAliasType):
246	        origin = typing.get_origin(origin.__value__)
247	    return tp is np.ndarray or origin is np.ndarray
248	
249	
250	def _decode_array(_tp: Any, data: Any) -> np.ndarray[Any, Any]:
251	    array = np.asarray(data)
252	    if array.dtype.kind == "f":
253	        return array.astype(np.float32)
254	    if array.dtype.kind not in "biu":
255	        raise TypeError(f"{data!r} is not a numeric array")
256	    return array
257	
258	
259	def _decode_generic(tp: Any, data: Any) -> Any:
260	    origin, args = typing.get_origin(tp), typing.get_args(tp)
261	    is_mapping = isinstance(origin, type) and issubclass(origin, Mapping)
262	    if not isinstance(data, dict if is_mapping else list):
263	        raise TypeError(f"{tp!r} can't hold {data!r}")
264	    if is_mapping:
265	        return {decode(args[0], k): decode(args[1], v) for k, v in data.items()}
266	    if origin is list or (len(args) == 2 and args[1] is Ellipsis):
267	        items = [decode(args[0], d) for d in data]
268	        return items if origin is list else tuple(items)
269	    if len(args) != len(data):
270	        raise TypeError(f"{data!r} does not have {len(args)} items")
271	    return tuple(decode(a, d) for a, d in zip(args, data, strict=True))
272	
273	
274	def _decode_scalar(tp: Any, data: Any) -> Any:
275	    if tp is Path:
276	        return Path(_checked(str, data))
277	    if tp is datetime:
278	        return datetime.fromisoformat(_checked(str, data))
279	    if tp is timedelta:
280	        return timedelta(seconds=_checked(float, data))
281	    if tp is float:
282	        return float(_checked(float, data))
283	    if tp in {int, str, bool}:
284	        return _checked(tp, data)
285	    raise TypeError(f"no decoder for {tp!r}")
286	
287	
288	def _checked(tp: type, data: Any) -> Any:
289	    numeric = tp is float and isinstance(data, int)
290	    if (isinstance(data, bool) and tp is not bool) or not (isinstance(data, tp) or numeric):
291	        raise TypeError(f"{data!r} is not {tp.__name__}")
292	    return data
293	
294	
295	_DECODERS: list[tuple[typing.Callable[[Any], bool], typing.Callable[[Any, Any], Any]]] = [
296	    (lambda tp: isinstance(tp, type) and dataclasses.is_dataclass(tp), _decode_dataclass),
297	    (lambda tp: typing.get_origin(tp) in {types.UnionType, typing.Union}, _decode_union),
298	    (lambda tp: typing.get_origin(tp) is typing.Literal, _decode_literal),
299	    (_is_array, _decode_array),
300	    (lambda tp: typing.get_origin(tp) is not None, _decode_generic),
301	]

2	name: dataviz
3	description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md`.
4	---
5	
6	# Data Visualization
7	
8	A chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns "make it look
9	good" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather
10	than by taste.
11	
12	**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form
13	heuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design
14	system supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a
15	diverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);
16	the method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the
17	reference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your
18	brand, read that file's structure and substitute its values - touch nothing else.
19	
20	> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**
21	> Never eyeball whether a palette is colorblind-safe - run `scripts/validate_palette.js`.
22	
23	## The procedure - do these in order
24	
25	Color comes LAST. Most bad charts pick colors first.
26	
27	1. **Pick the form.** What is the data's job - magnitude, identity, polarity, a
28	   single headline, change-over-time? The job picks the chart type, and sometimes
29	   the answer is *not a chart* (a stat tile or hero number). -> `references/choosing-a-form.md`
30	2. **Assign color by the job it does.** Categorical (identity), sequential
31	   (magnitude), diverging (polarity), or status (state) - each has one rule.
32	   Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled. -> `references/color-formula.md`
33	3. **VALIDATE the palette - run the script, don't reason about Delta E.**
34	   `node scripts/validate_palette.js "<hex,hex,...>" --mode light` (relative to
35	   this skill's base directory - or load it as `<script type="module">` in the
36	   chart's own page, where it reads
37	   `data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report). It returns
38	   pass/fail on the lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation,
39	   the normal-vision floor, and contrast. Fix anything that FAILs before continuing. Re-run for
40	   `--mode dark` with that mode's surface.
41	4. **Apply mark specs & spacers.** Thin marks, 4px rounded data-ends anchored to
42	   the baseline, 2px lines, >=8px markers, a 2px surface gap between fills (stacked
43	   segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring on overlapping marks,
44	   selective direct labels. -> `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`
45	5. **Add the hover layer - by default.** An HTML/SVG chart *is* interactive; ship
46	   a crosshair+tooltip on line/area and a per-mark hover tooltip on bar/dot/cell.
47	   The only form that skips it is a bare stat tile with no plot. Hit targets bigger
48	   than the mark; filters in one row above the charts. -> `references/interaction.md`
49	6. **Final accessibility pass.** For >= 2 series a legend is always present and <= 4
50	   are also direct-labeled (a single series needs no legend box - the title names
51	   it), so identity is never color-alone; a table view exists; dark mode is **selected** - its own
52	   steps from the same ramps, validated against the dark surface, not an automatic
53	   flip; texture is available for the CVD/print/forced-colors case.
54	7. **Render it and look at it.** The validator checks color, not layout - open or
55	   screenshot the output and eyeball it for label collisions, geometry, and overflow
56	   before calling it done.
57	
58	Then check the result against **`references/anti-patterns.md`** - it is the catalog
59	of what goes wrong. If your chart matches an entry, it's wrong.
60	
61	## Non-negotiables (true in every design system)
62	
63	- **Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled.** A 9th series is never a
64	  generated hue - it folds into "Other," small multiples, or composite encoding.
65	- **One axis.** Never a dual-axis chart (two y-scales). Two measures of different
66	  scale -> two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base. *(This is the
67	  #1 chart mistake - see anti-patterns.)*
68	- **Color follows the entity, never its rank.** A filter that changes the series
69	  count must not repaint the survivors.
70	- **Sequential = one hue, light->dark. Diverging = two hues + a neutral gray
71	  midpoint.** Never a rainbow; never a hue at the diverging midpoint.
72	- **Run the validator before shipping any categorical palette.** CVD Delta E >= 8 is the
73	  target (OKLab ×100); 6-8 is a floor that is legal ONLY with secondary encoding. A
74	  normal-vision floor below 15 is a hard FAIL - full-color readers can't tell the
75	  pair apart; re-step it on the adjacent pairlist (secondary encoding does not excuse
76	  this one); under `--pairs all` cut series or facet instead - see check 4. A contrast WARN
77	  obligates visible labels or a table view - it is not dismissable.
78	- **Thin marks; a legend always present for >= 2 series (none for one), with
79	  selective direct labels (never a number on every point); recessive grid/axes.**
80	- **Text wears text tokens, never the series color** - values, labels, and legends
81	  stay in primary/secondary/muted ink; a colored mark beside them carries identity.
82	- **Status colors are reserved** (good/warning/serious/critical) and never reused
83	  for "series 4"; they ship with an icon + label, never color alone.
84	
85	## Plugging in a design system
86	
87	The method is invariant; only these parameters change per system. The reference
88	instance - every value filled in - is `references/palette.md`.
89	
90	| Parameter | What the system provides |
91	|---|---|
92	| **Ramps** | the hue scales (named steps) the palette draws from |
93	| **Categorical theme** | the fixed hue order (a named theme); default + alternates |
94	| **Sequential hue** | the default single hue for magnitude |
95	| **Diverging pair** | two warm/cool poles + a neutral midpoint |
96	| **Status palette** | good / warning / serious / critical - steps distinct from categorical |
97	| **Texture fill** | one directional hand-drawn fill, used at 45° / 135° |
98	| **Surfaces** | light & dark chart-surface colors (the validator needs these) |
99	| **Filter controls** | date-range & dimension controls (behavioral spec in `interaction.md`) |
100	
101	To onboard a new system: fill those rows, feed its ramps to the validator, and let
102	it snap each slot to the nearest passing step. Structure and rules stay as written.

1	# Reference palette
2	
3	This is the **reference instance** of the data-viz method: every parameter the
4	method needs, filled in with a validated default palette. The rest of the skill
5	is system-agnostic - **to target your brand, substitute this file's values** and
6	re-run the validator. Nothing else changes.
7	
8	## How to use these values
9	
10	Everything below is plain hex. In an HTML chart, **define the slots you use as
11	CSS custom properties in a local `<style>` block** at the top of the file, then
12	reference them by role throughout - so the light/dark values swap in one place,
13	and the chart body is written against roles rather than raw hex:
14	
15	```css
16	.viz-root {
17	  color-scheme: light;
18	  --surface-1:      #fcfcfb;   /* chart surface */
19	  --text-primary:   #0b0b0b;
20	  --text-secondary: #52514e;
21	  --series-1:       #2a78d6;   /* categorical slot 1 */
22	  /* ...only the roles this chart uses */
23	}
24	@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
25	  :root:where(:not([data-theme="light"])) .viz-root {
26	    color-scheme: dark;
27	    --surface-1:      #1a1a19;
28	    --text-primary:   #f0efec;
29	    --text-secondary: #c3c2b7;
30	    --series-1:       #3987e5;
31	  }
32	}
33	:root[data-theme="dark"] .viz-root {
34	  color-scheme: dark;
35	  --surface-1:      #1a1a19;
36	  --text-primary:   #f0efec;
37	  --text-secondary: #c3c2b7;
38	  --series-1:       #3987e5;
39	}
40	```
41	
42	Declare the dark values under both scopes as above - the media query covers
43	the OS setting; the `data-theme` scope covers the viewer's theme toggle,
44	which must win both ways (the `:not(...)` guard lets a light stamp beat
45	OS-dark; `:where()` keeps the media block below the toggle scope).
46	
47	## Categorical palette
48	
49	Both modes are selected. The dark column is the same eight hues stepped for the
50	dark surface, not a separate palette:
51	
52	| Slot | Hue | Light | Dark |
53	|------|-----|-------|------|
54	| 1 | blue | `#2a78d6` | `#3987e5` |
55	| 2 | orange | `#eb6834` | `#d95926` |
56	| 3 | aqua | `#1baf7a` | `#199e70` |
57	| 4 | yellow | `#eda100` | `#c98500` |
58	| 5 | magenta | `#e87ba4` | `#d55181` |
59	| 6 | green | `#008300` | `#008300` |
60	| 7 | violet | `#6250d6` | `#9085e9` |
61	| 8 | red | `#e34948` | `#e66767` |
62	
63	This order passes every hard gate in both modes on the default *adjacent*
64	pairlist (stacks, bars, lines): worst adjacent CVD Delta E 9.1 light / 8.4 dark
65	(OKLab ×100, >=8 target), worst adjacent normal-vision Delta E 19.6 light / 19.3
66	dark (>=15 floor). Under `--pairs all` (scatter, bubble, choropleth, small
67	multiples) the full eight cannot clear the floors - with all 28 pairs in
68	play no ordering can (the pairlist no longer depends on order), and
69	re-stepping is off the table by the documented-palette rule - so those
70	chart forms carry a series cap: **the first three slots validate all-pairs

"""Learning curves with a min-max band and baseline lines (LOG-03 to LOG-05)."""

from collections.abc import Sequence
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
from matplotlib.axes import Axes
from matplotlib.figure import Figure
from numpy.typing import NDArray

from rllab.core import BaselineMeans, Output, WorldSpec
from rllab.runlog import Run

STEPS_LABEL = "environment steps"
# The dataviz skill's reference palette (light mode): categorical slot 1 and the chart chrome.
SERIES = "#2a78d6"
SURFACE = "#fcfcfb"
INK = "#0b0b0b"
SECONDARY = "#52514e"
MUTED = "#898781"
GRID = "#e1e0d9"
AXIS = "#c3c2b7"


def learning_curve(
    runs: Sequence[Run], baselines: BaselineMeans, out: Path, *, measure: str | None = None
) -> Output:
    figure = draw_curves(runs, baselines, measure)
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    figure.savefig(out)
    figure.savefig(out.with_suffix(".svg"))
    return Output(out, "chart", tuple(run.record.config.name for run in runs))


def draw_curves(runs: Sequence[Run], baselines: BaselineMeans, measure: str | None) -> Figure:
    """One panel per team (or one for `measure`): mean line, min-max band, baseline lines."""
    if not runs:
        raise ValueError("no runs to chart")
    spec = runs[0].record.spec
    panels = _panels(spec, measure)
    figure = Figure(figsize=(6.4 * len(panels), 4.2), facecolor=SURFACE, layout="constrained")
    axes = figure.subplots(1, len(panels), squeeze=False)[0]
    for ax, (team, label) in zip(axes, panels, strict=True):
        steps, values = _series(runs, team, measure)
        _draw_band(ax, steps, values, f"{team}: {label}, {len(runs)} runs")
        if measure is None:
            _draw_baseline(ax, baselines.random[team], "random play", "--", MUTED)
            _draw_baseline(ax, baselines.rule[team], "rule-based", ":", SECONDARY)
        _style(ax, label)
    return figure


def _panels(spec: WorldSpec, measure: str | None) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """(team, y-axis label) per panel: each team's score, or the declared measure's team."""
    if measure is None:
        return [(team.name, team.score_name) for team in spec.teams]
    declared = [m for m in spec.measures if m.name == measure]
    if not declared:
        raise ValueError(f"{spec.world} declares no measure {measure!r}")
    return [(declared[0].team, measure)]


def _series(
    runs: Sequence[Run], team: str, measure: str | None
) -> tuple[NDArray[np.int64], NDArray[np.float64]]:
    """The evaluation steps every run has, and each run's value there (runs x steps)."""
    by_run = [
        {p.step: p.scores[team] if measure is None else p.measures[measure] for p in run.evals()}
        for run in runs
    ]
    steps = sorted(set.intersection(*(set(values) for values in by_run)))
    rows = [[values[step] for step in steps] for values in by_run]
    return np.array(steps, dtype=np.int64), np.array(rows, dtype=np.float64)


def _draw_band(
    ax: Axes, steps: NDArray[np.int64], values: NDArray[np.float64], title: str
) -> None:
    ax.fill_between(
        steps, values.min(axis=0), values.max(axis=0), color=SERIES, alpha=0.18, linewidth=0,
        label="min–max range",
    )
    ax.plot(steps, values.mean(axis=0), color=SERIES, linewidth=2, label="mean")
    ax.set_title(title, color=INK, loc="left")


def _draw_baseline(ax: Axes, value: float, label: str, style: str, color: str) -> None:
    ax.axhline(value, color=color, linestyle=style, linewidth=1.5, label=label)
    ax.annotate(
        label, (1.0, value), xycoords=("axes fraction", "data"), xytext=(-4, 4),
        textcoords="offset points", ha="right", color=SECONDARY, fontsize=8,
    )


def _style(ax: Axes, label: str) -> None:
    ax.set_facecolor(SURFACE)
    ax.set_xlabel(STEPS_LABEL, color=SECONDARY)
    ax.set_ylabel(label, color=SECONDARY)
    ax.grid(color=GRID, linewidth=0.8)
    ax.tick_params(colors=MUTED)
    for side in ("top", "right"):
        ax.spines[side].set_visible(False)
    for side in ("left", "bottom"):
        ax.spines[side].set_color(AXIS)
    ax.legend(frameon=False, labelcolor=SECONDARY, fontsize=8, loc="upper left")

        evals = tuple(

            )
            for step, score in zip(STEPS, scores, strict=True)
        )
        config = replace(run.record.config, name=f"run-s{i}", seed=i)

    return line

    (band,) = [c for c in ax.collections if isinstance(c, PolyCollection)]
    ys = band.get_paths()[0].vertices[:, 1]
